hints.content:
The greatest common factor of $6x^3$, $8x^2$, and $-4x$ is $2x$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

Now we need to factor $2x$ out of $6x^3+8x^2-4x$.

options.explanation:
We find the prime factors of each term:

$\begin{align}
6x^3&=\blueD{(2)}(3)\goldD{(x)}(x)(x)
\\\\
8x^2&=\blueD{(2)}(2)(2)\goldD{(x)}(x)
\\\\
-4x&=(-1)\blueD{(2)}(2)\goldD{(x)}
\end{align}$

The greatest common factor is the product of all the shared parts:

$\blueD{(2)}\goldD{(x)}=2x$
